title: Offline caption workflow: relationships and review state

sections.title: Trace the review loop before treating a package as approved
sections.sub: One offline working snapshot of 12 imaginary exhibit captions. No execution or publication is authorized.

sections.title: The offline caption review loop
sections.description: Catalog facts enter Draft, which checks names and requests human Review. Review may return edits or pass approved captions to a Local package.
sections.caption: Source: caption-register, nodes and relationships. Claim: report-architecture. Dashed is presentation only, not a weaker-evidence label.

sections.title: Review status of 12 captions
sections.description: The mutually exclusive statuses cover all 12 captions. Corrected and Already clear have completed review; Pending review has not.
sections.caption: Source: caption-register, statuses and status_meaning. Claim: report-counts. These are fictional counts, not production quality metrics.

sections.title: What follows, and what does not
items: Observation [report-counts]: 7 corrected plus 3 already clear equals 10 reviewed captions; 2 remain pending.
Supplied rule and inference [report-gate]: all 12 must finish review for a complete approved package. The 2 pending captions mean that gate is not met.
Qualification [report-limit]: the source supplies no timing, defect-rate comparison or evidence that the loop improves quality.
A local package is not publication. This report does not execute the workflow.

rows.title: Does the feedback arrow prove that review improves caption quality?
rows.body: No. It documents an allowed relationship, not a measured effect. See report-limit.

rows.title: Can all 12 captions be treated as an approved package?
rows.body: No. Only 10 have completed review; 2 are still pending. See report-gate.

rows.status: Fictional authored evidence; not independently verified
